title: Investigate intermittent 502/504 spikes from proxy keepalive exhaustion; implement graceful retry coordination
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Multiple customers reported intermittent 502/504 errors and long tail timeouts during bursts of traffic over the last 48 hours. These errors correlate with elevated connection churn on the fronting proxy layer and an increase in sockets in CLOSE_WAIT/WAIT state. Initial evidence points to exhaustion of proxy keepalive slots and subsequent request failures when the proxy cannot establish a backend connection in time. This ticket tracks investigation, short-term mitigations, and a long-term fix that coordinates retries gracefully to avoid amplification while restoring customer traffic.
comments: 2025-02-18 - Asha Patel: Customer escalations (acct: ledgerx, acct: atlas-inc) started at ~10:12 UTC. Observed 0.7% 5xx rate peaking to 3.2% for 20 minutes. Created this ticket to centralize investigation and comms.

2025-02-18 - Marco Rivera: Collected tcpdump & netstat samples from two affected hosts. Noted many connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT for >120s; proxy config had keepalive timeout at 120s and max_idle_conns_per_host at 100. Opening deeper tracing for client latencies and backend accept queue.

2025-02-19 - Jamie Nguyen (SRE): Deployed temporary increase of proxy worker threads and bumped max_idle_conns_per_host to 300 in the EU cluster for affected tenants. Immediate reduction in 5xx spike but increased memory on proxies. Rollback scheduled after stabilization.

2025-02-19 - Marco Rivera: Reproduced locally with load-generator that simulates slow client bodies. When clients hold connections open (slow upload), the proxy's connection pool saturates and new request fronting results in 502. The backend accepts but proxy times out waiting for a free worker due to queue limits.
2025-02-20 - Security: No evidence of malicious traffic patterns. Traffic appears legitimate (long-polling chat clients + mobile clients on flaky networks). Marked security_review_required=false.

2025-02-21 - Marco Rivera: Implemented mitigation A (short-term): add per-tenant soft concurrency limit and immediate circuit to return 429 for excess non-idempotent requests to prevent blocking downstream. Deployed to staged and one canary region.

2025-02-22 - Product (Talia Gomez): Communicated with top affected customers: provided status update, mitigation timeline, and ask for request patterns (uploads/long polling). Customers requested sticky solution before EOW.

2025-02-24 - Marco Rivera: Drafted patch to SDK and gateway that introduces a retry-coordination token for idempotent retries, preventing retry storms during transient backend pressure. Patch at https://github.com/redwood-inference/proxy/pull/1842 (WIP).
2025-02-25 - Asha Patel: Preparing postmortem runbook and customer update template. Scheduling post-incident review for 2025-03-05.

2025-02-25 - Marco Rivera: Updated plan: roll out coordinated-retry in three phases (SDK soft-roll, gateway opt-in flag, proxy-side enforcement) and add metrics to track 'retry-token' acquisition failures. Target full rollout by 2025-03-03.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 5xx rate for impacted tenants returns to baseline (<0.2%) under same reproduced load; 2) retry coordination prevents >50% of client retries during proxy pressure; 3) no significant latency regression (p95 increase <10ms) after rollout; 4) playbook created for future similar incidents and customers updated.
implementation_notes: Short-term actions: increase proxy idle slots for canary, enable per-tenant soft limits, notify customers. Medium-term: implement retry-token coordination, add telemetry for 'backpressure_rejections' and 'retry_token_failures', and provide SDK updates to honor 'do-not-retry' header for non-idempotent endpoints. Long-term: explore dynamic connection pool autoscaling and faster TCP cleanup for CLOSE_WAIT via socket tuning and graceful-kill of stale connections.
qa_plan: 1) Synthetic test harness that reproduces slow-client behavior with varying concurrency; 2) Canary rollout to 5% of traffic with dashboarding for 5xx, p95, and retry-token failures; 3) Run game-day that intentionally saturates proxy to validate graceful degradation.
post_incident_actions: Schedule postmortem (2025-03-05), consolidate logs into incident archive, update runbooks with new thresholds and remediation steps, create customer-facing summary for impacted tenants. Evaluate whether to convert this mitigation into a permanent default for hosted clusters.
next_steps: 1) Finish PR #1842 and add unit/integration tests (Marco) 2) Push SDK opt-in for coordinated retries and call out in changelog (DevX) 3) Add dashboard panels for retry-token and connection-pool saturation (SRE) 4) Customer comms draft and legal signoff (PM).
notes: Avoid using broad retry blacklists; prefer coordinated tokens and backoff jitter. Keep customers informed when throttles are enabled. For Dedicated/private customers consider offering a tunable policy rather than hard defaults.
